THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 438 OF  CR.P.C PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN THE  EVENT OF HIS ARREST IN CRIME NO.98/2022 OF HUNASAGI POLICE  STATION, PENDING ON THE FILE OF ADDL. CIVIL JUDGE & J.M.F.C  SHORAPUR, FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECITONS  498(A), READ WITH SECTION 34 OF I.P.C AND SECTIONS 3 & 4 OF  D.P. ACT.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

1  -2-  CRL.P No. 200142 of 2023  ORDER Heard Sri S.B. Sangolagi, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Sharanabasappa M. Patil,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State.
2. It is the case of the prosecution that the father of the deceased lodged a complaint stating that he performed the marriage of his daughter on 20.04.2018 with accused No.1.
It is stated that at the time of marriage, they have given dowry as per the request of his son-in-law and his parents.
The couple blessed with two children.
They were cordial for six months.
Thereafter, there was a quarrel between his daughter and her husband and in-laws.
The husband, in-laws and the present petitioner used to demand dowry frequently and used to quarrel with the deceased in connection with dowry.
In spite of repeated panchayats and also instructions given in that regard to take care of her, they did not mend their ways and used to harass the deceased in one or other pretext.

It is further stated that, on 16.12.2022, his daughter had been to his parents' house and informed regarding the demand of dowry and again on 17.02.2022 returned to the matrimonial home, at that time, the petitioner, in-laws and husband have scolded his daughter and insulted her that, she did not brought dowry from her parents' house.
It is further stated that respondent No.2 has received a message from the in-laws of the deceased that his daughter died in the matrimonial home.
Thereafter, the complainant and his relatives had been to the house of the in-laws and lodged a complaint against his son-in-law and his parents and the present petitioner.

The police have registered the case in Crime No.98/2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A- 304B read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3.
It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is the husband of sister of accused No.1.
He is the resident of Aski village and he has been falsely implicated in this case in order to harass and take revenge, the false case has been registered since he is a government servant.
On careful reading of the entire complaint, there are omnibus allegations made out against the petitioners.
The petitioner is the Government employee and having deep root in the society.
He will abide the conditions imposed by this Court, in the event of his release on bail and co-operate with the investigation as and when required.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State vehemently opposed the bail application stating that there are prima facie allegations made out against the petitioner.
The alleged offences are heinous in nature and punishable with imprisonment for life.
Hence, if the anticipatory bail is granted, it will lead a wrong message to the society and public at large.
Hence, it is not appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the documents available Mainuddin Jamadar @ Mainuddin S/O Basha ... vs The State on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92280884/
2 on records and also the orders of the Trial Court, it appears that the petitioner is remotely connected with the deceased.

After having considered the submissions and also perused the averments made in the complaint, it is appropriate to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner, as the learned counsel for the petitioner has made out case to grant anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.98/2022 of Hunasagi Police Station.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within one month from today and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.

The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses;
d. The petitioner shall appear before the Trial Court on all dates of hearing.
